entry.title: Valve Updates Steam Review Process to Address Submission Surge
entry.content:
Links: theverge.com | steamcommunity.com

Valve is adjusting its Steam game submission workflow to manage a significant rise in store and page review requests. Due to this volume, current review times have reached up to 12 business days, a departure from the standard 3-5 day window.

The company is introducing new checklist requirements to minimize re-reviews caused by basic functional issues. These updates include requiring developers to run their games through the Steam client for at least five minutes and ensuring that achievements and necessary redistributables, such as DirectX, are properly configured.

entry.title: Rami Ismail Discusses Lessons Learned From Returning to Game Development
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com

Acclaimed indie developer Rami Ismail is returning to active game development with the turn-based strategy game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, developed alongside publisher Mystic Forge and studio Aesthetician Labs. In interviews, Ismail noted that the current industry landscape has grown significantly more brutal and risk-averse since his time co-owning Vlambeer.

To adapt to modern economic pressures and avoid traditional studio instability, Ismail adopted a flexible, project-based team structure rather than maintaining a permanent company. Designing a strategy game also required shifting away from his past focus on rapid, action-oriented prototyping toward long-term balance, leading to the creation of custom progression systems to help players navigate complex tactical choices.

entry.title: Apple Begins Beta Testing Apple Watch Audio Intelligence Features
entry.content:
Links: techcrunch.com

Apple has begun beta testing its new Audio Intelligence features for the Apple Watch, rolling them out to developers via the iOS 27.3 update. Initially announced for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, the suite includes four opt-in tools: sound recognition, song identification via Shazam, live conversation rewinds, and high-level conversation recaps.

The conversational features, Live Rewind and Siri Recaps, process audio using a combination of on-device S11 chip hardware, a secure enclave on the paired iPhone, and Apple’s Private Cloud Compute without saving raw audio or generating word-for-word transcripts. Live Rewind allows users to view a 15-second text snippet of recent speech by double-pressing the digital crown, while Siri Recaps summarizes meetings and discussions into concise bullet points that automatically delete after seven days if not saved.

entry.title: Apple Reports Inventory Surge Amid Rising Memory Chip Costs
entry.content:
Links: techcrunch.com | apple.com | hacker news

Apple reported that its inventory grew 154.3% year-over-year to $14.54 billion in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, driven largely by efforts to stockpile computer memory. During the earnings call, CEO John Ternus and COO Sabih Khan attributed downward pressure on the company's December quarter gross margin forecasts to unprecedented memory chip costs that are expected to continue rising.

The rising component costs and supply constraints also impacted product availability, contributing to weaker-than-expected iPad sales of $6.2 billion for the quarter. To secure supply, Apple's manufacturing purchase obligations increased by $33 billion from June to the September quarter, while executives declined to rule out further device price increases.

Store representatives indicated via social media that the surge is driven by generative AI tools, though the platform noted that downloads and purchases have not experienced a corresponding increase.

While Itch.io features optional AI disclosure tags and quality guidelines regarding truthful tagging, the platform does not mandate disclosure for a page to be published. The influx of automated content mirrors similar challenges faced by other digital storefronts, such as Valve addressing a rise in AI-copied games on Steam.

In an interview for Nintendo's "Ask the Developer" series, Aonuma noted that many current team members have only worked on recent titles and may lack firsthand experience with the original game.

The modern Zelda series has shifted from Ocarina of Time's linear, dungeon-focused progression toward the open-air exploration style seen in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. entry.title: Enabling Google Cast Support on a Samsung Q800A Soundbar
entry.content:
Links: codon.org.uk | lobsters

Matthew Garrett detailed a technical process for enabling Google Cast support on a US-model Samsung Q800A soundbar, which lacks the feature natively despite its presence on Australian variants. By extracting the firmware from a secondhand unit's eMMC storage, he identified a hidden Samsung Debug Bridge (sdb) interface that could be activated via network and USB configurations.

Once root access was established, he bypassed regional restrictions by altering the system country code, manually provisioning cryptographic keys into the soundbar's Trustzone environment, and updating the setup configuration endpoint. While the modification successfully exposed the device to local Cast clients, the regional configuration mismatch caused conflicts with SmartThings home integration.

entry.content:

Having succeeded Tim Cook, Ternus highlighted his deep roots at the company and his commitment to maintaining Apple's core design and engineering culture.

During the discussion, Ternus addressed the company's approach to artificial intelligence, asserting that Apple aims to organically integrate AI into secure and safe user experiences rather than pursuing technology for its own sake. While acknowledging the expanded responsibilities of running a major corporation, including high-level policy and services, Ternus reaffirmed that his primary passion remains deeply tied to hardware development.
